name: BelovedOne
note: Live Kuwait-HQ'd baby/kids retailer (since 2015, Avenues Mall store plus full e-commerce with cart) carrying ~500+ SKUs across clothing, toys, decor, bath, bags, and jewelry. The 'narrow, low-repeat boutique' basis is contradicted by the broad multi-category catalog, which clears the substantiality and repeat-purchase gates.

name: Beauty Gallery Qatar
note: bg-qa.com returns 502/503 (the server exists but the backend is erroring), not a non-existent domain, so the 'no live site' call is shaky for what reads as an approved-category beauty retailer in-scope for Qatar. Could not confirm a working storefront or HQ because the site would not render and the search budget was exhausted.

name: Gift Shed
note: giftshed.com does not resolve (no DNS, ENOTFOUND), independently confirming the dead-site call. No country on file and a generic gift-shop name (a borderline narrow category), with no findable live successor, so it defaults OUT per Gate 7.

name: Fantasy World
note: Misfiled as 'building_materials': fantasyworldtoys.com is a live Kuwait toy retailer (est. 1996, 7 stores, full cart/checkout, thousands of SKUs). Toys are an approved general-merchandise category and the operating entity is Kuwait-HQ'd.

name: Dimos Furniture | ديموس اثــــاث
note: Misfiled as 'building_materials': Dimos is a Riyadh-HQ'd consumer furniture retailer (Bin Hadi Investment Group) with showrooms in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam and a live online store (sofas, bedroom, living, outdoor, decor). Furniture/home is approved and it clears scale.

name: ALKAFFARY GROUP
note: Riyadh-HQ'd home-furnishings retailer since 1951 with 70+ stores plus online (carpets, rugs, flooring, furniture, home decor, wallpaper) and a presence on noon. It is retail-led and diversified well beyond carpets, so the narrow/low-repeat and mixed-conglomerate concerns do not hold; the Alkaffary Projects contracting arm is a non-disqualifying separate line under the corrected Gate 2 / Gate 6.

name: FirstCry Middle East
note: Gate 1 correctly fails: firstcry.sa is run by Indian parent BrainBees Solutions (HQ Pune), which is funding KSA outlets and a warehouse from its IPO proceeds. This is a foreign-parent local ccTLD storefront, matching the Ferns N Petals exclusion precedent.

name: LaScala Furniture Company
note: lascalafurniture.com is an inquiry-based brochure site for a bespoke/contract furniture manufacturer and self-described 'supplier of luxury furniture' with no cart, prices, or checkout. Fails on manufacturing/B2B (Gate 2) and lack of a real transactional digital channel (Gate 4).

name: L'ATELIER DE L'ART
note: ideahouse.com.sa is a Riyadh bespoke-furniture atelier handling made-to-order pieces, interior fit-outs, and aviation/marine projects on an inquiry basis. That is an interior fit-out / bespoke-project model (Gate 2 excluded, no consumer e-commerce), so the exclusion holds.

name: Ikaf Arabian Company
note: The 'manufacturer, not retail' basis is overstated: ikaf.net is live (403 bot-block, not dead) and runs its own multi-region branded thobe/apparel e-commerce, an approved category. But the dominant model is manufacturing plus wholesale/export (sold widely via third-party retailers) and I could not confirm the D2C catalog is substantial enough to clearly clear Gate 5, so it is genuinely borderline.

name: Maya Interiors
note: mayainteriors.com returns 503 and the name indicates an interior-design firm, an excluded B2B service (Gate 2), with no evidence of a consumer home/furniture retail store. Could not surface a qualifying retail model, so the exclusion stands.

name: Masco Saudi Arabia
note: Jeddah-HQ'd stationery/office-supplies business running a genuine D2C store at mascoonline.com (individual customers, prices, 90-day returns, free delivery over 99 SAR) alongside a wholesale/own-brand arm. Under the corrected Gate 2 the wholesale line is a separate fact; the dedicated retail arm plus approved category (stationery) qualify it.

name: METRO BRAZIL
note: Gate 1 hard-fail confirmed: Metro Brazil launched in Sao Paulo (2017) and moved its regional HQ to Dubai CommerCity (2021); neither is Saudi Arabia. It is a Brazil-origin, UAE-run e-commerce platform, so the Saudi-tagged account fails the in-country HQ test.

name: Lines Ideas
note: linesideas.com is a Riyadh-HQ'd B2B HORECA supplier equipping cafes and restaurants (syrups, flavors, machines, tools; Giffard brand). Its buyers are businesses, not consumers, and there is no dedicated consumer retail arm, so the B2B-distribution exclusion (Gate 2) holds.

name: MINISO Saudi Arabia
note: Misfiled as 'building_materials': miniso.sa is a live Saudi variety/lifestyle retailer operated by MINISO Saudi Arabia (a Riyadh-HQ'd local franchise entity, storefront on Salla) with physical stores nationwide and hundreds of SKUs. Approved category, in-country operating entity (the Cenomi-style Gate 1 pass), clears scale.

name: La Maison Doree
note: Misfiled as 'automotive': lamaisondoree.com is a Riyadh-HQ'd furniture and home-decor e-commerce retailer plus showroom (secure checkout, returns, broad catalog across furniture, lighting, tableware, decor), with B2B/design only a secondary line. Approved category, Saudi HQ, real digital channel.

name: Mumuso Qatar
note: The domain on file, mumuso.com, is the Chinese parent's (Shanghai Mumu Life Trading) global brand site (503 when checked), not a Qatar-operated storefront; the Qatar presence is franchise mall stores selling online only via third-party platforms. Fails Gate 1 (foreign-parent brand with no in-country operating-entity storefront), unlike MINISO which has its own Saudi entity and site.

name: Nahdi
note: The 500 'dead' call was a transient/bot error: nahdi.sa is live and Nahdi is Saudi Arabia's largest retail pharmacy chain (Jeddah-HQ'd, 1,151 stores, live online pharmacy). Retail pharmacy chains are the explicit approved exception, so this is a clear qualifier.

name: Mogahwi Stationery & Office Equipment
note: Misfiled as 'automotive': mogahwi.com.kw (Almuqahwi Library Co, est. 1942) is a Kuwait stationery/art-supplies retailer with physical stores (Shuwaikh, Sharq) and a live online shop. Stationery is an approved, repeat-purchase category and the entity is Kuwait-HQ'd.

name: Noon com
note: The 'dead' call is wrong (noon.com is the region's largest live marketplace), but the exclusion stands on Gate 1: Noon is a Dubai/UAE-based marketplace (Mohamed Alabbar), so despite a large app it fails the in-country geography gate, which Gate 5b app-rescue cannot override.

name: Oloom and Hikam Bookstore
note: oloomhikam.com does not resolve (no DNS), but a bookstore is an approved, repeat-purchase category and only the dead-site gate blocks it. Could not complete the mandated domain-move search because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so whether a live successor exists is genuinely unresolved.

name: Brandatt
note: The 'DEAD 000' basis is wrong: brandatt.com is live and returns 403 (bot-blocked), not dead. But the site would not render and the search budget was exhausted, so the business model or HQ country could not be determined; qualification is unresolved.

name: Pet Barn
note: petbarnkw.com is a substantial Kuwait consumer pet retailer (2 stores, online cart/checkout, grooming, mobile app, shop-by-brand). Its B2B/wholesale arm does not disqualify it under the corrected Gate 2 (the Petzone precedent); pet supplies are an approved category and the retail operation stands on its own.

name: Razin Furniture Co.
note: razin.com is a Riyadh furniture/joinery manufacturer and contract supplier (6,000 sqm factory) serving contractors, hotels, hospitals, government, and palaces on a project basis, with a portfolio/'Projects' site and no consumer cart. Manufacturing/contract-furniture (Gate 2) with no real consumer e-commerce (Gate 4), so the exclusion holds.
